# phi-scan: synthetic
#
# Page excerpts in the shape PyMuPDF produces for the three ACIP/ files. Those
# are not guideline documents at all, they are browser print-to-PDF captures of
# CDC schedule pages, and the header they carry is what says so: a print
# timestamp, the page title, the source URL and an "n of m" folio.
#
# **This file has now been wrong in both directions, and the reason is the same
# one both times: the shape is the test.** It first put the stamp on a line of
# its own, was corrected to the folded form because pypdf welds the title in
# after the timestamp, and is corrected back here because #83 moved the extractor
# to PyMuPDF and the four parts land on four lines again. Verified against
# ACIP/Recommended Vaccinations for Adults ... CDC.pdf on 2026-08-16 rather than
# reasoned about -- which is what the previous round of this failed to do.
#
# The consequence for the corpus is visible and worth knowing: a capture now
# contributes three page-repeated lines rather than one, because the stamp, the
# title and the URL each repeat on their own. The folio does not; it differs per
# page, which is #100's subject and not this file's.
#
# The timestamp is date-shaped, which is why this file declares the pragma above.
# It is a browser artifact from a public CDC page and no patient is anywhere near
# it, but the shape layer cannot know that and should not have to.
#
# Four pages, form-feed separated, header lines stripped by the loader. CDC
# content is federal and public domain, so unlike the AHA excerpts this one could
# have been copied verbatim; the body is still trimmed to what the tests need.
Recommended Vaccinations for Adults
